title: Circular security with random opening from weaker assumptions
subfield: Indistinguishability obfuscation: foundational assumptions
open: Can the specialized "circular security with random opening" property used in lattice-based obfuscation be derived from an ordinary circular-security assumption via an explicit reduction? In other words, is this strengthened property genuinely necessary, or does conventional circular encryption security already imply it?
status: The 2025 construction of Hsieh–Jain–Lin (*Lattice-Based Post-Quantum iO from Circular Security with Random Opening Assumption*, ePrint 2025/390) introduces the circular-security-with-random-opening property as a specialized assumption; ordinary circular encryption security is known not to be an interchangeable assumption for this purpose.
solved_when: An explicit reduction is exhibited deriving the circular-security-with-random-opening property from a standard circular-security assumption (or a convincing argument shows no such reduction exists).
why: It determines whether a proposed simplification of the assumption basis for indistinguishability obfuscation is substantive or merely a relabeling of a stronger assumption.
key_works: Hsieh–Jain–Lin (2025), *Lattice-Based Post-Quantum iO from Circular Security with Random Opening Assumption*, ePrint 2025/390.

title: xiO from one-way functions
subfield: Exponentially efficient, decomposable, and succinct obfuscation
open: Can exponentially efficient indistinguishability obfuscation (xiO) be built from one-way functions alone, so that obfuscated circuits of size \(2^{(1-\varepsilon)n}\operatorname{poly}(\lambda,|C|)\) are achievable for some constant \(\varepsilon>0\)? Formally, the goal is an xiO construction whose only hardness assumption is one-way functions, with the stated output-size bound.
status: The 2016 xiO framework (Lin–Pass–Seth–Telang, *Indistinguishability Obfuscation with Non-trivial Efficiency*, ePrint 2016/006) isolates nontrivial compression as the core requirement, but an OWF-only construction remains unresolved. Related directions include minimum circuit size and computational compression.
solved_when: A construction of xiO from one-way functions is given, producing obfuscations of size \(2^{(1-\varepsilon)n}\operatorname{poly}(\lambda,|C|)\) for a constant \(\varepsilon>0\).
why: Even partial truth-table compression would yield a powerful intermediate cryptographic primitive, giving a stepping stone toward obfuscation from minimal assumptions.
key_works: Lin–Pass–Seth–Telang (2016), *Indistinguishability Obfuscation with Non-trivial Efficiency*, ePrint 2016/006.

title: Polynomial-security xiO-to-iO lifting
subfield: Exponentially efficient, decomposable, and succinct obfuscation
open: Can polynomially secure exponentially efficient indistinguishability obfuscation (xiO) be upgraded to full polynomial-time iO, without assuming subexponential security of xiO or of any auxiliary primitive it relies on? Formally: does a lifting theorem exist that pays only a polynomial security loss?
status: The foundational lifting theorem of Lin–Pass–Seth–Telang (2016), *Indistinguishability Obfuscation with Non-trivial Efficiency* (DOI: 10.1007/978-3-662-49387-8_17), achieves the xiO-to-iO upgrade only by assuming subexponential hardness; no polynomial-security lifting is known.
solved_when: A proof (or construction) is given that transforms any polynomially secure xiO scheme into a polynomial-time iO scheme, where neither the xiO scheme nor any auxiliary building block is assumed to satisfy subexponential security.
why: It would turn weak, merely polynomially secure obfuscation constructions into full-fledged iO, making such constructions far more consequential and dramatically lowering the hardness assumptions needed for iO.
key_works: Lin–Pass–Seth–Telang (2016), *Indistinguishability Obfuscation with Non-trivial Efficiency*, DOI: 10.1007/978-3-662-49387-8_17.

title: Decomposable obfuscation directly from plain LWE
subfield: Exponentially efficient, decomposable, and succinct obfuscation
open: Can general-purpose decomposable obfuscation be built directly from plain LWE, with only polynomial security loss? That is, an obfuscation scheme whose decomposable structure suffices for the usual applications, resting on ordinary LWE alone rather than stronger assumptions.
status: Liu–Zhandry (2017/2021), *Decomposable Obfuscation*, DOI: 10.1007/s00145-021-09400-4, provide a framework showing what decomposability enables, but this does not itself establish the assumption-specific construction from plain LWE. Related directions include compositional circuit transformations and succinct encodings.
solved_when: A construction of general-purpose decomposable obfuscation is given, based on plain LWE, with security proven via a polynomial reduction (polynomial security loss).
why: It would deliver useful obfuscation applications earlier, without waiting for the full plain-LWE indistinguishability obfuscation problem to be resolved.
key_works: Liu–Zhandry (2017/2021), *Decomposable Obfuscation*, DOI: 10.1007/s00145-021-09400-4.

bib.title: Decomposable obfuscation directly from plain LWE

title: Conjunction obfuscation from ordinary Ring-LWE
subfield: Stronger obfuscation notions, auxiliary information, and leakage
open: Can a conjunction obfuscator be built and proven secure from ordinary Ring-LWE alone, without any extra entropic assumption? Failing that, can we exactly characterize the distributions for which plain Ring-LWE suffices?
status: The existing route (Cousins et al. 2017/2018, *Implementing Conjunction Obfuscation under Entropic Ring LWE*, DOI: 10.1109/SP.2018.00007) is implemented but relies on an entropic variant of Ring-LWE, leaving the question of removing that assumption open. Related work concerns learning conjunctions under nonuniform distributions.
solved_when: Either a conjunction-obfuscation construction is proven secure under standard Ring-LWE with no additional entropic assumption, or a precise characterization is given of the distributions under which ordinary Ring-LWE suffices (and the entropic assumption is shown necessary outside that class).
why: It would turn one of the more concrete restricted-obfuscation approaches into a construction resting on a standard, well-studied assumption, tightening its security story.
key_works: Cousins et al. (2017/2018), *Implementing Conjunction Obfuscation under Entropic Ring LWE*, DOI: 10.1109/SP.2018.00007.

title: Unbounded-collusion public-key FE from plain LWE
subfield: Functional encryption for general circuits
open: Can we build public-key functional encryption for all polynomial-size circuits, tolerating arbitrarily many functional-key requests, from the plain Learning with Errors assumption? Formally, construct unbounded-collusion FE for general circuits under ordinary LWE with no auxiliary obfuscation-style assumptions.
status: General FE and bounded-collusion FE exist, but the combination of a clean assumption (ordinary LWE) with unrestricted collusion remains unresolved. See Boneh–Sahai–Waters (2011), *Functional Encryption: Definitions and Challenges*, ePrint 2010/543.
solved_when: A construction is given of public-key FE supporting every polynomial-size circuit and an arbitrary polynomial number of functional-key queries, proved secure under plain LWE alone.
why: It would deliver expressive encrypted computation — computing on encrypted data for general circuits — without relying on general obfuscation assumptions.
key_works: Boneh–Sahai–Waters (2011), *Functional Encryption: Definitions and Challenges*, ePrint 2010/543.

bib.title: Unbounded-collusion public-key FE from plain LWE

title: Unbounded-collusion secret-key FE from OWFs
subfield: Functional encryption for general circuits
open: Construct secret-key FE for general circuits from OWFs without fixing the number of issued functional keys at setup.
status: Minimal-assumption bounded-collusion results do not resolve the unbounded regime.
why: It would move a powerful class of selective-decryption capabilities toward minimal assumptions.
key_works: Boneh–Sahai–Waters (2011), *Functional Encryption: Definitions and Challenges*, DOI: 10.1007/978-3-642-19571-6_16.

title: General public-key FE from arbitrary PKE
subfield: Functional encryption for general circuits
open: Can unbounded-collusion functional encryption for general circuits be built starting solely from ordinary public-key encryption, with no additional assumptions? Non-black-box constructions are explicitly permitted.
status: Recent decentralized FE obtains bounded-collusion functionality from PKE but uses FE for the unbounded-collusion case; see Goyal–Yadugiri (2025/2026), *Decentralized Multi-Authority Functional Encryption with Malicious Authorities from Standard Assumptions*, ePrint 2025/412.
solved_when: A construction of general public-key FE secure against unbounded collusion is given, whose only underlying primitive is a standard PKE scheme.
why: It asks whether ordinary encryption already contains the power of arbitrary selective decryption.
key_works: Goyal–Yadugiri (2025/2026), *Decentralized Multi-Authority Functional Encryption with Malicious Authorities from Standard Assumptions*, ePrint 2025/412.

bib.title: General public-key FE from arbitrary PKE

title: Succinct-encryption general FE from plain LWE
subfield: Functional encryption for general circuits
open: Can we build functional encryption for general circuits, secure under the plain Learning with Errors assumption, whose encryption algorithm and ciphertext size do not depend on a bound on the functions that may later be evaluated? Formally, the encryption circuit and ciphertext size should be succinct — independent of any a priori maximum function size.
status: Succinct encryption is a powerful strengthening of functional encryption: sufficiently secure FE with this property yields iO, as shown by Bitansky–Vaikuntanathan (2015/2018), *Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Functional Encryption*, ePrint 2015/163; DOI: 10.1145/3234511. No such construction from plain LWE is known.
solved_when: A general-circuit FE scheme is constructed from ordinary (plain) LWE in which encryption and ciphertext size avoid any dependence on a future maximum function size, with no additional assumptions beyond plain LWE.
why: It would let data be encrypted before the scale of future computations on it is known, and — since sufficiently secure FE with succinct encryption yields indistinguishability obfuscation — it offers a route to iO from a standard assumption.
key_works: Bitansky–Vaikuntanathan (2015/2018), *Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Functional Encryption*, ePrint 2015/163; DOI: 10.1145/3234511.

bib.title: Succinct-encryption general FE from plain LWE

title: Expressive registered ABE from plain LWE
subfield: Restricted FE, attribute-based encryption, and registration
open: Can we build attribute-based encryption with registration-based key management — no trusted authority holding a master secret — that supports expressive policies and tolerates malicious registrants, using only the plain Learning With Errors assumption? The goal is a construction achieving compact aggregation among users' independently registered keys without relying on stronger tools.
status: Existing registered constructions using pseudorandom functionalities (e.g., Pal–Schädlich–Tairi, 2025, ePrint 2025/967) can inherit additional evasive-assumption dependencies, so plain-LWE registered ABE of this expressive strength remains open.
solved_when: A registered ABE scheme for an expressive policy class is proven secure under plain LWE alone, supports malicious registration, and achieves compact key aggregation.
why: It would eliminate master-secret escrow in expressive ABE without reintroducing extraordinary assumptions such as evasive-lattice or obfuscation-style primitives.
key_works: Pal–Schädlich–Tairi (2025), *Registered Functional Encryption for Pseudorandom Functionalities from Lattices*, ePrint 2025/967.

bib.title: Expressive registered ABE from plain LWE

title: Witness encryption from OWFs
subfield: Witness encryption and conditional release
open: Construct NP witness encryption from arbitrary OWFs, allowing non-black-box methods.
status: WE dates to 2013; the general OWF-only standard-model construction remains unresolved.
why: It would greatly lower the foundation required for conditional cryptographic release.
key_works: Garg–Gentry–Sahai–Waters (2013), *Witness Encryption and Its Applications*, DOI: 10.1145/2488608.2488667.

title: A useful trilinear map from established assumptions
subfield: Multilinear maps and graded encodings
open: Construct a cryptographically useful trilinear map with efficient operations and a reduction to an independently studied assumption, rather than general iO.
status: The multilinear-form challenge predates candidate graded encodings and remains distinct from their existence.
why: Degree three already enables capabilities unavailable from ordinary pairings.
key_works: Boneh–Silverberg (2003), *Applications of Multilinear Forms to Cryptography*, ePrint 2002/080.

bib.title: A useful trilinear map from established assumptions

title: Polynomial-arity graded encodings from conventional assumptions
subfield: Multilinear maps and graded encodings
open: Can we construct graded encodings that support polynomially many multiplicative levels, with compact encodings, and whose security rests on a conventional cryptographic assumption rather than on the security of an ad hoc candidate?
status: Existing candidate constructions — notably Garg–Gentry–Halevi (2013), *Candidate Multilinear Maps from Ideal Lattices* (ePrint 2012/610) and Gentry–Gorbunov–Halevi (2015), *Graph-Induced Multilinear Maps from Lattices* (ePrint 2014/645) — have not become a broadly accepted standard-assumption solution.
solved_when: A construction is given whose number of multiplicative levels grows polynomially in the security parameter, whose encodings remain compact, and whose security is proved under a standard, well-studied assumption.
why: Polynomial arity is the resource that many of the most ambitious applications of multilinear maps — such as general program obfuscation — need; without it, those applications remain out of reach.
key_works: Garg–Gentry–Halevi (2013), *Candidate Multilinear Maps from Ideal Lattices*, ePrint 2012/610; Gentry–Gorbunov–Halevi (2015), *Graph-Induced Multilinear Maps from Lattices*, ePrint 2014/645.

bib.title: Polynomial-arity graded encodings from conventional assumptions

title: Secure reusable public zero testing
subfield: Multilinear maps and graded encodings
open: Can a multilinear-encoding scheme support a public zero-test that an adversary cannot exploit, even when the adversary constructs the encodings being tested and adaptively issues repeated, correlated zero-test queries?
status: Zero-testing interfaces are a central source of attacks on candidate multilinear encodings; see Cheon–Han–Lee–Ryu–Stehlé (2015), *Cryptanalysis on the Multilinear Map over the Integers and its Related Problems*, ePrint 2014/906.
solved_when: A scheme is given whose public zero-testing procedure remains secure — i.e., reveals nothing about the encodings' hidden algebraic structure — under adversarially constructed inputs and arbitrarily many repeated, correlated tests, with a proof of this security.
why: Zero testing is the operation that makes graded encodings useful, yet it is precisely the interface through which known attacks extract the hidden structure; without a reusable, adversarially secure zero test, applications of multilinear maps rest on sand.
key_works: Cheon–Han–Lee–Ryu–Stehlé (2015), *Cryptanalysis on the Multilinear Map over the Integers and its Related Problems*, ePrint 2014/906.

title: Security of GGH15-style maps beyond zeroizing models
subfield: Multilinear maps and graded encodings
open: Is any useful GGH15-style graded-encoding construction secure against all efficient adversaries, or does an attack exist outside the zeroizing class currently analyzed? A proof (or break) beyond the zeroizing-attack model would settle whether the surviving candidate family has real cryptographic security rather than only a narrow, syntactically restricted notion of it.
status: The state of the art is security against zeroizing attacks (Bartusek–Guan–Ma–Zhandry, 2018, *Return of GGH15: Provable Security Against Zeroizing Attacks*, ePrint 2018/511), which is strictly narrower than full cryptographic security; no result currently resolves security against unrestricted efficient adversaries.
solved_when: Either a proof of security for a useful GGH15-style construction against unrestricted efficient attacks is given, or a concrete attack outside the protected zeroizing class is demonstrated.
why: It would establish whether a surviving candidate family of multilinear maps has a defensible security margin, or expose that its security holds only under the artificially restricted zeroizing model.
key_works: Bartusek–Guan–Ma–Zhandry (2018), *Return of GGH15: Provable Security Against Zeroizing Attacks*, ePrint 2018/511.

bib.title: Security of GGH15-style maps beyond zeroizing models

title: Private DCR-based CPRFs beyond bounded Waring rank
subfield: Constrained pseudorandom functions
open: Can the DCR-based private constrained PRF construction be extended to substantially broader polynomial predicates, so that the constrained key no longer needs to grow with a large Waring decomposition of the constraint polynomial?
status: The 2025–2026 construction of Behera–Meyer–Orlandi–Roy–Scholl (ePrint 2025/230) supports puncturing and bounded-Waring-rank functionality; nothing yet goes beyond these.
solved_when: A private CPRF from DCR is given for a class of polynomial constraints going beyond puncturing and bounded Waring rank, without key size growing with a large Waring decomposition of the constraint.
why: It would expand the space of useful private constraints reachable without invoking full indistinguishability obfuscation.
key_works: Behera–Meyer–Orlandi–Roy–Scholl (2025/2026), *Privately Constrained PRFs from DCR: Puncturing and Bounded Waring Rank*, ePrint 2025/230.

bib.title: Private DCR-based CPRFs beyond bounded Waring rank

title: Expressive post-quantum key-homomorphic CPRFs
subfield: Constrained pseudorandom functions
open: Can we build constrained pseudorandom functions that are simultaneously key-homomorphic, support general expressive constraint classes, and remain secure against full collusion — all under post-quantum assumptions? Formally, the goal is an instantiation where constraining and key homomorphism coexist for arbitrary expressive constraints with security holding against unboundedly many colluding constraint holders.
status: Current key-homomorphic capabilities are limited to restricted constraint families and do not settle the general expressive regime; see Langrehr (2025/2026), *Limits on the Power of Constrained PRFs and Identity-based Cryptography*, ePrint 2025/1338.
solved_when: A construction is given that achieves key homomorphism and general expressive constraints simultaneously, with full collusion resistance, proven secure under post-quantum assumptions.
why: Such a primitive would support distributed and proactively refreshed constrained capabilities, enabling constrained PRF power to be shared and evolved across parties without re-trusting a single holder.
key_works: Langrehr (2025/2026), *Limits on the Power of Constrained PRFs and Identity-based Cryptography*, ePrint 2025/1338.

title: Characterizing copy-protectable function families
subfield: Copy protection and secure software leasing
open: Which natural function families admit copy protection? A structural characterization — necessary and sufficient conditions tying protectability to properties of the function family itself — is sought, moving beyond the goal of protecting every unlearnable family.
status: Conditional impossibility results rule out the blanket goal of copy-protecting every unlearnable family, while known positive families leave a large classification problem open. Key work includes Ananth–La Placa (2020/2021), *Secure Software Leasing*, arXiv:2005.05289.
solved_when: A theorem gives checkable structural conditions on a function family that are both necessary and sufficient for copy protection, and these conditions classify the known positive families.
why: It would explain what kinds of software can fundamentally be protected, separating the protectable from the inherently clonable.
key_works: Ananth–La Placa (2020/2021), *Secure Software Leasing*, arXiv:2005.05289.

title: One-shot signatures from plain LWE
subfield: Uncloneable encryption, quantum money, and one-shot capabilities
open: Can one-shot signatures — signature schemes where signing consumes the secret key so a second signature cannot be produced — be constructed from the plain Learning With Errors assumption alone? In particular, can this be done without resorting to subexponentially secure indistinguishability obfuscation?
status: Standard-model one-shot signatures now exist from stronger assumptions, so their bare existence is no longer open; the open question is achieving them from weaker, ordinary assumptions. Key work: Shmueli–Zhandry (2025/2026), *On One-Shot Signatures, Quantum vs Classical Binding, and Obfuscating Permutations*, ePrint 2025/486.
solved_when: A construction of one-shot signatures is given whose only underlying assumption is standard (plain) LWE, with no use of subexponential-security iO; a proof of security in the standard model completes the solution.
why: It would place self-consuming authorization capabilities on a cleaner, more plausible cryptographic foundation, replacing the current reliance on heavy obfuscation machinery.
key_works: Shmueli–Zhandry (2025/2026), *On One-Shot Signatures, Quantum vs Classical Binding, and Obfuscating Permutations*, ePrint 2025/486.

title: Public quantum money from plain LWE
subfield: Uncloneable encryption, quantum money, and one-shot capabilities
open: Can we build publicly verifiable, reusable quantum money in the standard model from plain LWE, without relying on indistinguishability obfuscation or an idealized group-action model? Formally, the goal is a construction whose security reduces to the ordinary Learning With Errors assumption.
status: Existing constructions achieve public-key quantum money from standard assumptions only in the generic model — Doliskani (2025/2026), *Public-Key Quantum Money From Standard Assumptions (In The Generic Model)*, ePrint 2025/092 — and these generic-model results under named assumptions do not establish the standard-model target.
solved_when: A construction of reusable, publicly verifiable quantum money exists whose security is proven in the standard model under plain LWE, with no iO or generic/idealized group-action model assumption.
why: It would ground public quantum money in a familiar, widely trusted post-quantum assumption, making the primitive plausibly deployable rather than dependent on heavy or idealized machinery.
key_works: Doliskani (2025/2026), *Public-Key Quantum Money From Standard Assumptions (In The Generic Model)*, ePrint 2025/092.

bib.title: Public quantum money from plain LWE

title: Explicit instantiations of group-action quantum money
subfield: Uncloneable encryption, quantum money, and one-shot capabilities
open: Can any explicit family of group actions be shown secure as the basis for group-action quantum money against quantum adversaries that exploit the specific structure of the action, rather than treating it as a generic black box — or does every candidate admit such a nongeneric break?
status: Generic group-action security does not automatically validate a concrete action; no explicit family is currently confirmed secure against nongeneric quantum attacks. Key works include Zhandry (2024), *Quantum Money from Abelian Group Actions*, DOI: 10.4230/LIPIcs.ITCS.2024.101, and Doliskani (2025), ePrint 2025/092.
solved_when: A concrete group-action family is exhibited with a proof of quantum money security against nongeneric (non-generic-model) quantum attacks, or an explicit candidate is broken by such an attack.
why: This is the direct instantiation problem behind a promising money framework: without a concrete, provably secure action, the framework remains an abstraction with no implementable scheme.
key_works: Zhandry (2024), *Quantum Money from Abelian Group Actions*, DOI: 10.4230/LIPIcs.ITCS.2024.101; Doliskani (2025), ePrint 2025/092.

bib.title: Explicit instantiations of group-action quantum money

title: Quantum lightning from conventional assumptions
subfield: Uncloneable encryption, quantum money, and one-shot capabilities
open: Can quantum lightning — a publicly verifiable protocol whose output states are uncloneable in the strongest sense — be constructed from an assumption that was already established for other purposes, rather than from multicollision-style or idealized assumptions tailored to the construction?
status: Lightning remains stronger than ordinary public quantum money and has its own construction frontier; the state of the art is Zhandry's construction (Zhandry 2019/2021, *Quantum Lightning Never Strikes the Same State Twice*, arXiv:1711.02276; DOI: 10.1007/s00145-020-09372-x).
solved_when: A publicly verifiable quantum lightning scheme exists whose security reduces to a conventional, independently established hardness assumption, with no reliance on specialized multicollision assumptions or idealized models.
why: It would yield publicly recognizable unique quantum resources without a trusted mint, unlocking one-shot and uncloneable capabilities that currently lack such foundations.
key_works: Zhandry (2019/2021), *Quantum Lightning Never Strikes the Same State Twice*, arXiv:1711.02276; DOI: 10.1007/s00145-020-09372-x.

title: Unleveled FHE from plain LWE
subfield: Fully homomorphic encryption: construction foundations
open: Can fully homomorphic encryption with no pre-set depth bound — supporting arbitrary polynomial-depth circuits — be built from ordinary Learning With Errors, using a fixed setup and without assuming circular security?
status: Leveled FHE without bootstrapping, as in Brakerski–Gentry–Vaikuntanathan (2012/2014), *(Leveled) Fully Homomorphic Encryption without Bootstrapping*, ePrint 2011/277, does not settle the unrestricted-depth target, since the parameters must grow with the evaluation depth.
solved_when: A compact FHE scheme is constructed from plain LWE whose public parameters are fixed once (not depending on the target depth) and which supports evaluation of arbitrary polynomial-depth circuits, without relying on a circular-security assumption.
why: It would remove an extra foundational assumption from general-purpose computation on encrypted data.
key_works: Brakerski–Gentry–Vaikuntanathan (2012/2014), *(Leveled) Fully Homomorphic Encryption without Bootstrapping*, ePrint 2011/277.

title: Adaptive-corruption logarithmic-overhead RAM-MPC
subfield: RAM-model MPC and oblivious memory
open: Can the three-party RAM-MPC setting with logarithmic overhead be made secure against adaptive malicious adversaries, without assuming erasures? More precisely, can parties be corrupted at any point during the computation — including after state has accumulated — while preserving the same logarithmic-overhead guarantee currently achieved only against static corruptions?
status: DORAM Revisited (Falk–Noble–Ostrovsky–Shtepel–Zhang (2023), *DORAM Revisited: Maliciously Secure RAM-MPC with Logarithmic Overhead*, ePrint 2023/578) establishes the static-corruption malicious baseline for this regime.
solved_when: A three-party RAM-MPC protocol is exhibited that withstands adaptive malicious corruption, requires no idealized erasures, and retains logarithmic overhead.
why: Persistent private services build up state over time, and a protocol that only tolerates static corruptions leaves that accumulated state exposed to an adversary who strikes later.
key_works: Falk–Noble–Ostrovsky–Shtepel–Zhang (2023), *DORAM Revisited: Maliciously Secure RAM-MPC with Logarithmic Overhead*, ePrint 2023/578.

title: Succinct HSS from polynomial-ratio LWE
subfield: Homomorphic secret sharing, garbling, and preprocessing
open: Can succinct homomorphic secret sharing be built from LWE with only a polynomial ratio between the modulus and the noise? That is, can the superpolynomial modulus-to-noise requirement in the Abram–Roy–Scholl (2024) construction be relaxed to a conventional polynomial ratio?
status: Succinct HSS currently has an LWE route via Abram–Roy–Scholl (2024), *Succinct Homomorphic Secret Sharing* (ePrint 2024/814), but the construction requires a superpolynomial modulus-to-noise ratio — a parameter qualification that limits its assumption strength.
solved_when: A succinct HSS construction is given whose security reduces to LWE with a polynomial modulus-to-noise ratio, replacing the superpolynomial ratio currently required.
why: It would place succinct HSS on a standard lattice assumption with a realistic parameter profile, making compact distributed computation more practical and better trusted.
key_works: Abram–Roy–Scholl (2024), *Succinct Homomorphic Secret Sharing*, ePrint 2024/814.

title: Succinct constant-party HSS for general circuits
subfield: Homomorphic secret sharing, garbling, and preprocessing
open: Can homomorphic secret sharing for a constant number of parties support arbitrary circuits — not just restricted computation models — with both compact shares and small output communication, assuming only plain LWE? A satisfying construction should work directly on general circuits rather than first converting them into large branching-program representations.
status: Succinct HSS constructions exist only for restricted computation models, and these do not settle efficiency for general circuits. Abram–Roy–Scholl (2024), *Succinct Homomorphic Secret Sharing*, DOI: 10.1007/978-3-031-58751-1_11.
solved_when: A construction exists that handles general circuits under plain LWE with succinct shares and succinct output communication, without going through large branching-program representations.
why: It would make distributed encrypted computation fully expressive without paying large communication costs.
key_works: Abram–Roy–Scholl (2024), *Succinct Homomorphic Secret Sharing*, DOI: 10.1007/978-3-031-58751-1_11.

bib.title: Succinct constant-party HSS for general circuits

title: Post-quantum rate-1 arithmetic garbling
subfield: Homomorphic secret sharing, garbling, and preprocessing
open: Can rate-1 arithmetic garbling be achieved under conventional post-quantum assumptions, matching the efficiency of the DCR-based constructions?
status: The state of the art is the DCR-based rate-1 arithmetic garbling of Meyer–Orlandi–Roy–Scholl (2024), *Rate-1 Arithmetic Garbling from Homomorphic Secret-Sharing*, ePrint 2024/820, but DCR-based constructions do not provide post-quantum security.
solved_when: A garbling scheme for arithmetic computations achieves rate-1 communication (output size comparable to the plaintext computation) and comparable efficiency to the DCR-based construction of Meyer–Orlandi–Roy–Scholl (2024), while being secure under a standard post-quantum assumption.
why: Communication-efficient arithmetic MPC currently rests on DCR, which fails against quantum attackers; a quantum-resistant replacement is needed to preserve these gains in a post-quantum world.
key_works: Meyer–Orlandi–Roy–Scholl (2024), *Rate-1 Arithmetic Garbling from Homomorphic Secret-Sharing*, ePrint 2024/820.

title: Constant-rate Boolean garbling under plain post-quantum assumptions
subfield: Homomorphic secret sharing, garbling, and preprocessing
open: Can Boolean circuits of size $s$ be garbled with communication (or preprocessing material) growing as $O(s)$ bits, under standard post-quantum assumptions? That is, can we achieve rate-1 garbling measured directly in Boolean circuit size, rather than by amortizing security costs into large arithmetic words?
status: Arithmetic rate-1 results do not automatically imply bit-level rate-1 garbling (cf. Meyer–Orlandi–Roy–Scholl (2024), ePrint 2024/820); the Boolean-circuit constant-rate case remains open.
solved_when: A garbling scheme exists for Boolean circuits of size $s$ producing garbled circuit and labels of total size $O(s)$ bits, with post-quantum security based on plain (standard) assumptions.
why: Many practical computations are dominated by short-word and Boolean operations, so arithmetic rate-1 results that only amortize over large words leave the dominant real-world cost uncovered.
key_works: Meyer–Orlandi–Roy–Scholl (2024), ePrint 2024/820.

bib.title: Constant-rate Boolean garbling under plain post-quantum assumptions

title: Collision-resistant hashing from arbitrary OWFs
subfield: Minimal assumptions, meta-complexity, and remaining post-quantum constructions
open: Construct collision-resistant hashing from arbitrary OWFs without stronger algebraic assumptions or an obfuscation helper.
status: Black-box barriers and conditional advances do not settle unrestricted constructions.
why: Collision resistance supports commitments, authentication, and succinct proofs.
key_works: Asharov–Segev (2015), *Limits on the Power of Indistinguishability Obfuscation and Functional Encryption*, ePrint 2015/341.

subfield: Minimal assumptions, meta-complexity, and remaining post-quantum constructions
open: Can oblivious transfer be constructed from any public-key encryption scheme, using purely classical means, without assuming extra algebraic structure or a completeness property on the encryption? More precisely: does arbitrary PKE imply classical OT, or is there a fundamental separation?

Key work: Gertner–Kannan–Malkin–Reingold–Viswanathan (2000), *The Relationship between Public Key Encryption and Oblivious Transfer*, DOI: 10.1109/SFCS.2000.892121.
solved_when: A proof that every public-key encryption scheme yields classical oblivious transfer (or a counterexample separating the two), with no additional algebraic or completeness assumption; black-box arguments alone do not suffice.
why: It asks whether all public-key encryption already enables general private computation, settling whether OT is strictly stronger than PKE among classical primitives.

title: Distributional collision resistance from OWFs
subfield: Minimal assumptions, meta-complexity, and remaining post-quantum constructions
open: Can distributional collision-resistant hash functions be constructed from arbitrary one-way functions, or is there an inherent barrier? A positive answer would show this relaxed collision notion, where the adversary must output a collision drawn from a prescribed distribution rather than an arbitrary one, is achievable under the minimal assumption of inversion hardness.
status: The only stated fact is that this weaker collision notion supports useful primitives not known from OWFs alone. Key work: Bitansky–Haitner–Komargodski–Yogev (2019), *Distributional Collision Resistance Beyond One-Way Functions*, DOI: 10.1007/978-3-030-17659-4_23.
solved_when: A construction of distributional collision-resistant hashing is given whose security reduces to the existence of arbitrary one-way functions; alternatively, the problem is resolved in the negative direction by an oracle or black-box separation showing one-way functions do not imply distributional collision resistance.
why: A solution would bridge part of the gap between inversion hardness and full collision resistance, potentially bringing primitives currently not known from OWFs alone — such as statistically hiding commitments — within reach of the minimal assumption.
key_works: Bitansky–Haitner–Komargodski–Yogev (2019), *Distributional Collision Resistance Beyond One-Way Functions*, DOI: 10.1007/978-3-030-17659-4_23.

title: Full-domain post-quantum trapdoor permutations from plain LWE
subfield: Minimal assumptions, meta-complexity, and remaining post-quantum constructions
open: Can one construct trapdoor permutations over their full domain from the plain Learning-with-Errors assumption alone, without invoking indistinguishability obfuscation? In other words, is there a post-quantum construction of full-domain trapdoor permutations resting only on standard LWE?
status: The domain qualification is no longer universally unresolved: full-domain trapdoor permutations have now been constructed, but from stronger obfuscation assumptions rather than plain LWE. The relevant construction appears in Shmueli–Zhandry (2025/2026), *On One-Shot Signatures, Quantum vs Classical Binding, and Obfuscating Permutations*, ePrint 2025/486.
solved_when: An explicit construction of full-domain trapdoor permutations is given, based solely on plain LWE and making no use of iO or stronger obfuscation assumptions, with a proof of correctness, one-wayness under LWE, and invertibility using the trapdoor.
why: It would restore a powerful reversible cryptographic tool — with all the classical applications of trapdoor permutations — under a conventional, well-studied post-quantum assumption rather than heavyweight obfuscation.
key_works: Shmueli–Zhandry (2025/2026), *On One-Shot Signatures, Quantum vs Classical Binding, and Obfuscating Permutations*, ePrint 2025/486.

title: Compact multiparty NIKE from plain post-quantum assumptions
subfield: Minimal assumptions, meta-complexity, and remaining post-quantum constructions
open: Can an arbitrary polynomial-size group of parties, each broadcasting just one announcement and with compact public material, noninteractively agree on a shared secret — using only ordinary post-quantum assumptions rather than heavy machinery?
status: Indistinguishability obfuscation gives a route under strong assumptions (Boneh–Zhandry, *Multiparty Key Exchange, Efficient Traitor Tracing, and More from Indistinguishability Obfuscation*, ePrint 2013/642, 2014/2017), but two-party post-quantum NIKE does not settle NIKE for arbitrary groups.
solved_when: A construction of multiparty NIKE for arbitrary polynomial-size groups with one announcement per participant and compact public material, based on standard (non-iO) post-quantum assumptions, with a proof of security.
why: It would let mutually distrustful groups establish shared secrets without any interactive coordination, a basic distributed-coordination capability currently out of reach from plain assumptions.
key_works: Boneh–Zhandry (2014/2017), *Multiparty Key Exchange, Efficient Traitor Tracing, and More from Indistinguishability Obfuscation*, ePrint 2013/642.

title: Adaptive-authority decentralized tracing
subfield: Traitor tracing and accountable broadcast
open: Can decentralized multi-authority traitor tracing be made secure when tracing authorities are corrupted adaptively — that is, after the system is deployed — without assuming erasures of previously secret state?
status: The 2026 construction of Datta–Schädlich–Tairi (*Decentralized Multi-Authority (Attribute-Based) Traitor Tracing*, ePrint 2026/1268) handles authority corruption only in the static model, where the set of corrupted authorities is fixed in advance.
solved_when: A decentralized multi-authority tracing construction exists with a proof of security against adaptive (post-deployment) authority corruption, replacing the current static-corruption model and avoiding any reliance on erasures.
why: Long-lived tracing systems must tolerate authorities compromised after deployment; without adaptive security, a single late compromise of an authority can undermine the entire tracing mechanism.
key_works: Datta–Schädlich–Tairi (2026), *Decentralized Multi-Authority (Attribute-Based) Traitor Tracing*, ePrint 2026/1268.

title: General-purpose iO from plain LWE
subfield: Indistinguishability obfuscation: foundational assumptions
open: Can general-purpose indistinguishability obfuscation be built from nothing more than ordinary, polynomially hard LWE? Concretely, construct iO for all polynomial-size Boolean circuits from plain LWE alone, without evasive, circular, equivocal, pairing, or knowledge-type assumptions.
status: General iO currently requires multi-assumption constructions; the 2025 lattice route of Cini–Lai–Woo (2025), *Lattice-based Obfuscation from NTRU and Equivocal LWE*, ePrint 2025/1129, still needs Equivocal LWE and NTRU-related machinery, building on the well-founded-assumptions approach of Jain–Lin–Sahai (2021), *Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Well-Founded Assumptions*, ePrint 2020/1003.
solved_when: A construction of iO for all polynomial-size Boolean circuits exists whose security reduces to standard polynomially hard LWE, with no additional assumptions of evasive, circular, equivocal, pairing, or knowledge type.
why: It would place general software obfuscation on a single, widely studied post-quantum foundation, replacing today's multi-assumption lattice constructions.
key_works: Jain–Lin–Sahai (2021), *Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Well-Founded Assumptions*, ePrint 2020/1003; Cini–Lai–Woo (2025), *Lattice-based Obfuscation from NTRU and Equivocal LWE*, ePrint 2025/1129.

title: General-purpose iO from one-way functions
subfield: Indistinguishability obfuscation: foundational assumptions
open: Can general-purpose indistinguishability obfuscation for circuits be constructed from nothing more than the existence of arbitrary one-way functions? Concretely, is there a construction (with genuinely non-black-box techniques and reductions) achieving iO under the sole assumption that one-way functions exist?
status: Black-box limitations are known — Asharov–Segev (2015), *Limits on the Power of Indistinguishability Obfuscation and Functional Encryption* (ePrint 2015/341) — but these do not establish an unrestricted impossibility theorem, leaving non-black-box approaches open.
solved_when: A construction of general circuit iO is given, proved secure by a reduction that assumes only the existence of one-way functions, with no stronger assumptions invoked anywhere in the proof.
why: Success would collapse the foundational cost of the entire obfuscation application ecosystem down to the minimal assumption in cryptography, settling how much structure iO truly requires.
key_works: Asharov–Segev (2015), *Limits on the Power of Indistinguishability Obfuscation and Functional Encryption*, ePrint 2015/341.

title: Unrestricted iO without subexponential hardness
subfield: Indistinguishability obfuscation: foundational assumptions
open: Can indistinguishability obfuscation for unrestricted (general) circuits be built from polynomially hard, independently studied assumptions? Formally, the goal is a construction that avoids complexity leveraging and hence does not require any primitive with subexponential security.
status: Progress has been made on polynomial-hardness for proof-restricted obfuscation, but this does not itself yield unrestricted iO from polynomially hard conventional assumptions. Key works include Jain–Lin–Sahai (2021), ePrint 2020/1003, and Dujmovic–Hsieh–Jain–Quach (2026), *How to use Polynomially-Hard iO: Turing Machine Obfuscation and More*, ePrint 2026/1636.
solved_when: A construction of unrestricted circuit iO is given whose security reduces to assumptions that are polynomially hard and independently studied, with no subexponential hardness requirement from complexity leveraging.
why: It would substantially shrink the gap between asymptotic existence results and meaningful, concrete security parameters, making iO plausibly instantiable in practice.
key_works: Jain–Lin–Sahai (2021), ePrint 2020/1003; Dujmovic–Hsieh–Jain–Quach (2026), *How to use Polynomially-Hard iO: Turing Machine Obfuscation and More*, ePrint 2026/1636.

title: Equivocal LWE from ordinary LWE
subfield: Indistinguishability obfuscation: foundational assumptions
open: Is Equivocal LWE no stronger than ordinary LWE — can it be reduced to standard LWE — or does an attack exist that breaks Equivocal LWE while leaving ordinary LWE intact?
status: Equivocal LWE was introduced as an additional assumption in the 2025 lattice-obfuscation construction; no reduction to ordinary LWE and no separating attack is known.
solved_when: Either a reduction establishes that any adversary breaking Equivocal LWE yields one breaking ordinary LWE, or an explicit attack is exhibited that separates the two assumptions.
why: This isolates and potentially removes a concrete dependency on one route toward plain-LWE indistinguishability obfuscation: if the assumptions are equivalent, the 2025 lattice-obfuscation construction rests on standard LWE alone; if they separate, a genuine barrier on that route is identified.
key_works: Cini–Lai–Woo (2025), *Lattice-based Obfuscation from NTRU and Equivocal LWE*, ePrint 2025/1129.

title: Non-lattice post-quantum iO
subfield: Indistinguishability obfuscation: foundational assumptions
open: Can general-purpose indistinguishability obfuscation be built from a post-quantum assumption family that is independently studied and does not rest on lattices — that is, an assumption whose hardness was investigated in its own right before being used for obfuscation, and that is not already equivalent to iO itself?
status: Existing well-founded constructions combine several ingredients, and recent lattice candidates do not supply the desired assumption diversity; the state of the art for well-founded iO remains the multi-ingredient approach of Jain–Lin–Sahai (2021), *Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Well-Founded Assumptions*, DOI: 10.1145/3406325.3451093. Potentially relevant directions include average-case decoding hardness and quantum algorithms for hidden algebraic structure.
solved_when: A construction of general iO is given that is provably post-quantum secure under a well-founded assumption family outside lattices, where the assumption is independently studied and not equivalent to obfuscation.
why: It would reduce dependence on correlated failures within a single mathematical platform; a break in the lattice family would not sink all known post-quantum iO.
key_works: Jain–Lin–Sahai (2021), *Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Well-Founded Assumptions*, DOI: 10.1145/3406325.3451093.

title: A defensible taxonomy of evasive-LWE assumptions
subfield: Indistinguishability obfuscation: foundational assumptions
open: Can the many variants of the evasive-LWE assumption be organized into a defensible taxonomy, so that for each combination of sampler access, public versus private coins, auxiliary information, and leakage conditions we know whether reductions are valid, explicit attacks exist, or the case is genuinely unresolved?
status: The 2025–2026 attacks of Hsieh–Jain–Lin (2025, ePrint 2025/390) and Huang–Hung–Yamada (2025/2026, *A Note on Obfuscation-Based Attacks on Private-Coin Evasive LWE*, ePrint 2025/421) invalidate several private-coin formulations, and nearby definitions cannot safely inherit one another's security.
solved_when: Every regime obtained by varying sampler access, coin privacy, auxiliary information, and leakage conditions is labeled as admitting a valid reduction, suffering an explicit attack, or provably open — with no unlabeled combinations.
why: It would prevent broken assumptions from reappearing under slightly changed notation, which is an acute risk since nearby definitions cannot safely inherit one another's security.
key_works: Hsieh–Jain–Lin (2025), ePrint 2025/390; Huang–Hung–Yamada (2025/2026), *A Note on Obfuscation-Based Attacks on Private-Coin Evasive LWE*, ePrint 2025/421.

title: Cryptanalysis of all-product LWE
subfield: Indistinguishability obfuscation: foundational assumptions
open: How secure is the all-product LWE assumption underlying path-factorized functional encryption? Concrete security estimates — or better, practical attacks — for this assumption are needed.
status: The assumption is introduced by Diamond iO (Suegami–Bottazzi–Park, 2025, revised 2026, *Diamond iO: Indistinguishability Obfuscation at Near Functional-Encryption Cost via Matrix Products*, ePrint 2025/236); the construction paper itself provides no independent cryptanalytic validation. Related lines of attack include tensor decomposition hardness and solving structured polynomial systems.
solved_when: Either a concrete security estimate for all-product LWE is established (with explicit parameters) or a cryptanalytic attack is demonstrated against it.
why: The assumption is a concentrated point of failure in an efficiency-oriented obfuscation proposal, so its untested hardness determines whether the construction rests on solid ground.
key_works: Suegami–Bottazzi–Park (2025, revised 2026), *Diamond iO: Indistinguishability Obfuscation at Near Functional-Encryption Cost via Matrix Products*, ePrint 2025/236.

title: Instantiating the pseudorandom-oracle step in efficient iO
subfield: Indistinguishability obfuscation: foundational assumptions
open: Can the pseudorandom-oracle component of an efficiency-oriented indistinguishability-obfuscation construction be replaced by an explicit standard-model primitive, keeping both the security proof and the asymptotic advantage intact? In other words, can the idealized oracle in this transformation be discharged by a concrete assumption rather than assumed?
status: The Diamond iO construction of Suegami–Bottazzi–Park (2025/2026) (ePrint 2025/236) achieves its transformation via pseudorandom-oracle-model machinery, and replacing that oracle with a standard-model primitive remains a separate, open obligation.
solved_when: The oracle-model step of the construction is realized by an explicit standard-model primitive, with the resulting obfuscator preserving the security and asymptotic efficiency of the original idealized-model construction.
why: An efficient transformation that relies on an idealized oracle model does not yet yield a deployable obfuscator; without the replacement, the efficiency gains remain unavailable in the standard model.
key_works: Suegami–Bottazzi–Park (2025/2026), *Diamond iO*, ePrint 2025/236.

title: Independently reproduced end-to-end general iO
subfield: Indistinguishability obfuscation: foundational assumptions
open: Can a general-purpose indistinguishability obfuscation candidate be implemented end-to-end at explicit, unrestricted parameters, with all costs measured? That is, an actual artifact whose generation time, evaluation time, peak memory, output size, and the cost of every assumed component are benchmarked and independently reproduced.
status: The Near-FE transformation cost is known, but this does not establish a practical end-to-end cost nor an independently validated security margin. The relevant candidate is Suegami–Bottazzi–Park (2025/2026), *Diamond iO*, ePrint 2025/236.
solved_when: An unrestricted iO candidate is implemented at explicit parameters, and an independent reproduction reports generation time, evaluation time, peak memory, output size, and per-component costs for every assumed component of the construction.
why: Such measurements would reveal whether current candidates are bottlenecked by a single component or by the entire construction, which no current analysis establishes.
key_works: Suegami–Bottazzi–Park (2025/2026), *Diamond iO*, ePrint 2025/236.

title: xiO from plain LWE
subfield: Exponentially efficient, decomposable, and succinct obfuscation
open: Can exponentially efficient, decomposable, succinct obfuscation (xiO) be built from the plain Learning with Errors assumption alone? That is, obtain nontrivially compressing xiO without relying on equivocal, evasive, or specialized circular assumptions.
status: New lattice obfuscation routes have not removed all additional assumptions, even when compression is treated as an intermediate goal. Key works: Lin et al. (2016), ePrint 2016/006; Cini–Lai–Woo (2025), ePrint 2025/1129.
solved_when: A construction of nontrivially compressing xiO is given whose security reduces to ordinary LWE, with no equivocal, evasive, or specialized circular assumptions used.
why: Such a construction would be a potentially more accessible milestone than directly constructing polynomial-time iO, opening a concrete path toward indistinguishability obfuscation from standard assumptions.
key_works: Lin et al. (2016), ePrint 2016/006; Cini–Lai–Woo (2025), ePrint 2025/1129.

title: The computational compression frontier
subfield: Exponentially efficient, decomposable, and succinct obfuscation
open: Which obfuscation goals survive compression? Determine the tight tradeoffs among obfuscation time, output length, input length, and assumption strength for computationally secure compressing obfuscation.
status: Current complexity classifications and statistical-security barriers leave multiple computational regimes unmatched; the state of the art is given by Asharov–Ephraim–Komargodski–Pass (2018/2022), *On the Complexity of Compressing Obfuscation*, ePrint 2018/552.
solved_when: The tradeoffs are characterized tightly — matching upper and lower bounds relating obfuscation time, output length, input length, and the computational assumptions required — so that no computational regime is left between the known classifications and statistical-security barriers.
why: A solution identifies which weak obfuscation goals are genuinely easier than full indistinguishability obfuscation, charting the terrain of achievable weaker primitives.
key_works: Asharov–Ephraim–Komargodski–Pass (2018/2022), *On the Complexity of Compressing Obfuscation*, ePrint 2018/552.

title: A semantic characterization of decomposable obfuscation
subfield: Exponentially efficient, decomposable, and succinct obfuscation
open: Can decomposability of an obfuscator be characterized purely by semantic properties, rather than by the syntax of particular constructions? A formal answer would give a definition under which an obfuscator qualifies as decomposable exactly when it satisfies those semantic conditions.
status: The decomposable-obfuscation framework of Liu–Zhandry (2017/2021), *Decomposable Obfuscation: A Framework for Building Applications of Obfuscation from Polynomial Hardness* (DOI: 10.1007/s00145-021-09400-4), supports important applications, but no complete classification of eligible obfuscators is known.
solved_when: A semantic criterion is formulated and shown to be equivalent to decomposability for obfuscators, yielding a complete classification of eligible obfuscators within the decomposable-obfuscation framework.
why: It would make application proofs less dependent on bespoke construction details, letting them rest on the semantic properties of whatever obfuscator is used.
key_works: Liu–Zhandry (2017/2021), *Decomposable Obfuscation: A Framework for Building Applications of Obfuscation from Polynomial Hardness*, DOI: 10.1007/s00145-021-09400-4.

title: Incrementally updatable obfuscation
subfield: Exponentially efficient, decomposable, and succinct obfuscation
open: Can an obfuscated program be updated after a small patch using work proportional only to the changed region, while still hiding unchanged secrets and any patch history beyond what is declared as leakage?
status: Decomposability alone is not an incremental-update security theorem. Key works: Liu–Zhandry (2017/2021), *Decomposable Obfuscation*, DOI: 10.1007/s00145-021-09400-4.
solved_when: A construction and security proof exist in which applying a patch to an obfuscated program costs work proportional to the changed region, and the update reveals nothing about unchanged secrets or the patch history beyond the declared leakage.
why: It would allow obfuscated software to be maintained and patched over time, rather than shipped as immutable releases.
key_works: Liu–Zhandry (2017/2021), *Decomposable Obfuscation*, DOI: 10.1007/s00145-021-09400-4.

title: Fully succinct unrestricted obfuscation without additional helpers
subfield: Exponentially efficient, decomposable, and succinct obfuscation
open: Can fully input-succinct unrestricted obfuscation be built from polynomially hard circuit iO alone, without separately assuming succinct witness encryption or suitable unique-proof succinct arguments?
status: Recent proof-restricted constructions identify additional ingredients (beyond iO) needed to achieve stronger succinctness.
solved_when: A construction of fully input-succinct unrestricted obfuscation is given, basing its security solely on polynomially hard circuit iO with no additional succinct-WE or unique-proof succinct-argument assumptions.
why: It would make the size of the obfuscated secret program largely independent of the eventual input-size bound.
key_works: Jain–Jin–Mathialagan–Paneth (2025/2026), *On Succinct Obfuscation via Propositional Proofs*, ePrint 2026/2009.

title: Proof-system dependence of obfuscation
subfield: Exponentially efficient, decomposable, and succinct obfuscation
open: Does strengthening the proof system used to define circuit equivalence — moving beyond PV-provable equivalence to stronger systems — actually increase the power of obfuscation, or does it merely change proof lengths and efficiency? In other words, is the attainable class of obfuscatable functions sensitive to the underlying proof system, or only the cost of the construction?
status: Modern proof-restricted obfuscation constructions explicitly depend on the chosen equivalence-proof system; the dependence is visible in the constructions of Jain et al. (2025/2026) (ePrint 2026/2009) and Dujmovic et al. (2026) (ePrint 2026/1636), but whether this dependence reflects power rather than efficiency remains open.
solved_when: A characterization exists showing either that obfuscation power is invariant across the relevant proof systems (with only proof length/efficiency varying), or that some stronger proof system strictly enlarges the class of obfuscatable functions relative to PV-provable equivalence.
why: A solution distinguishes a merely technical limitation of current constructions from a genuine hierarchy of cryptographic primitives indexed by proof strength.
key_works: Jain et al. (2025/2026), ePrint 2026/2009; Dujmovic et al. (2026), ePrint 2026/1636.

title: Practical equivalence certificates for proof-restricted obfuscation
subfield: Exponentially efficient, decomposable, and succinct obfuscation
open: Can we automatically generate succinct, machine-checkable equivalence proofs for the transformations a real obfuscating compiler performs, at a proof-generation cost comparable to compilation itself?
status: Current polynomial-hardness PViO advances — Dujmovic–Hsieh–Jain–Quach (2026), *How to use Polynomially-Hard iO*, ePrint 2026/1636 — establish cryptographic possibilities, but no production compiler yet supplies the necessary certificates.
solved_when: A production compiler for proof-restricted obfuscation emits succinct, checkable equivalence certificates for realistic compiler transformations, with proof-generation cost comparable to the cost of compilation.
why: It would connect proof-restricted obfuscation to real software development, turning cryptographic feasibility into a usable engineering artifact.
key_works: Dujmovic–Hsieh–Jain–Quach (2026), *How to use Polynomially-Hard iO*, ePrint 2026/1636.

title: Public-coin diO without knowledge assumptions
subfield: Stronger obfuscation notions, auxiliary information, and leakage
open: Can public-coin differing-inputs obfuscation be constructed from indistinguishability obfuscation together with conventional assumptions, without invoking KOALA or any other knowledge-style assumption?
status: An October 2026 preprint obtains public-coin diO from KOALA and iO (Chen–Vaikuntanathan (2026), *Public-coin Differing-input Obfuscation from KOALA and iO*, ePrint 2026/2346), leaving the removal of the knowledge-style assumption open.
solved_when: A construction of public-coin diO is given, basing its security on iO plus standard (non-knowledge) assumptions alone.
why: It would strengthen the obfuscation toolkit while avoiding assumptions that posit limits on what an adversary "knows," which are harder to formalize and justify.
key_works: Chen–Vaikuntanathan (2026), *Public-coin Differing-input Obfuscation from KOALA and iO*, ePrint 2026/2346.

title: The attainable auxiliary-input frontier for diO
subfield: Stronger obfuscation notions, auxiliary information, and leakage
open: For which classes of auxiliary-input samplers does differing-inputs obfuscation remain attainable? A complete answer would give, for each such class, a construction of differing-inputs obfuscation secure against it, together with a barrier showing the notion is unachievable for meaningfully stronger classes.
status: Broad formulations of auxiliary input are known to be implausible, following Garg–Gentry–Halevi–Wichs (2014), *On the Implausibility of Differing-Inputs Obfuscation and Extractable Witness Encryption with Auxiliary Input*, ePrint 2013/860; however, restricting the sampler can materially change the question, and a systematic map of this frontier remains open.
solved_when: A characterization of auxiliary-input generators is established, with matching constructions for every class in the characterization and impossibility (or implausibility) results for generators strictly beyond it.
why: It would replace the current ambiguous catch-all phrase "auxiliary-input security" with a usable, fine-grained classification that obfuscation constructions can be measured against.
key_works: Garg–Gentry–Halevi–Wichs (2014), *On the Implausibility of Differing-Inputs Obfuscation and Extractable Witness Encryption with Auxiliary Input*, ePrint 2013/860.

title: Structural classification of VBB-obfuscatable families
subfield: Stronger obfuscation notions, auxiliary information, and leakage
open: Which natural function families can be virtually-black-box obfuscated, and which structurally cannot? A characterization should give necessary and sufficient conditions under which a broad family of circuits admits VBB obfuscation.
status: Universal VBB obfuscation is impossible by Barak et al. (2001/2012), *On the (Im)possibility of Obfuscating Programs*, DOI: 10.1145/2160158.2160159; the unresolved task is classifying which families lie between the positive cases and the unobfuscatable examples, with connections to exact learning and structural classification of concept classes.
solved_when: A theorem (or family of theorems) giving necessary and sufficient structural conditions for a broad natural function family to admit VBB obfuscation, cleanly separating positive families from the unobfuscatable examples.
why: It would pinpoint exactly where the strongest intuitive form of software secrecy is achievable, and where it provably fails.
key_works: Barak et al. (2001/2012), *On the (Im)possibility of Obfuscating Programs*, DOI: 10.1145/2160158.2160159.

title: Obfuscation for approximately equivalent randomized programs
subfield: Stronger obfuscation notions, auxiliary information, and leakage
open: Can we obfuscate randomized programs whose output distributions are only approximately equal, so that security degrades in a controlled way with the approximation error and the number of times the obfuscated program is run?
status: Indistinguishability obfuscation for exactly equivalent programs does not automatically yield this guarantee, and any solution must remain compatible with the known impossibility of unrestricted virtual black-box obfuscation (Barak et al. 2001/2012; Jain et al. 2025/2026, ePrint 2026/2009).
solved_when: An obfuscation scheme exists for randomized programs that are close in output distribution, with a security guarantee that carries an explicit, quantitative dependence on both the approximation error and the number of evaluations.
why: Real probabilistic and numerical software rarely satisfies exact functional equivalence, so existing exact-notion obfuscators do not apply to it; such a scheme would extend obfuscation to this practical class of programs.
key_works: Barak et al. (2001/2012), *On the (Im)possibility of Obfuscating Programs*; Jain et al. (2025/2026), ePrint 2026/2009.

title: Stateful obfuscation with an explicit leakage boundary
subfield: Stronger obfuscation notions, auxiliary information, and leakage
open: Which natural families of stateful programs can be obfuscated so that their internal state stays hidden even under adaptive interactions, resets, and forks, under an explicitly declared leakage model?
status: Currently known stateless circuit-obfuscation results do not address state cloning, reset behavior, or leakage from persistent history, so the stateful case remains open. Foundational context is Barak et al. (2001/2012), *On the (Im)possibility of Obfuscating Programs*, DOI: 10.1145/2160158.2160159; related directions include resettable computation and information-flow security for state machines.
solved_when: A characterization is given of stateful program families obfuscatable in this sense — hiding internal state across adaptive interaction, reset, and fork — together with a specified leakage boundary under which the hiding is proven.
why: Most useful services are interactive and stateful, so obfuscation theory that only covers stateless circuits does not apply to them.
key_works: Barak et al. (2001/2012), *On the (Im)possibility of Obfuscating Programs*, DOI: 10.1145/2160158.2160159.

title: Sharp entropy thresholds for conjunction obfuscation
subfield: Stronger obfuscation notions, auxiliary information, and leakage
open: How little entropy can a conjunction (secret policy) have before known conjunction-obfuscation candidates become insecure? A precise answer would give the minimum entropy conditions under which these obfuscators remain secure, together with matching attacks when the entropy falls below that threshold.
status: Implementations under entropic Ring-LWE assumptions exist (Cousins et al. (2017/2018), *Implementing Conjunction Obfuscation under Entropic Ring LWE*, ePrint 2017/844), but security for arbitrary low-entropy conjunction distributions does not follow.
solved_when: A sharp entropy threshold is characterized: security proven for conjunction distributions meeting the bound, and explicit attacks demonstrated for distributions below it.
why: Real-world policies are frequently highly structured and nonuniform, so guarantees limited to high-entropy distributions may not cover the cases that actually arise in practice.
key_works: Cousins et al. (2017/2018), *Implementing Conjunction Obfuscation under Entropic Ring LWE*, ePrint 2017/844.

title: Standard-model extractable WE for restricted samplers
subfield: Stronger obfuscation notions, auxiliary information, and leakage
open: Can extractable witness encryption be built in the standard model for a well-specified class of samplers, such as public-coin or bounded-auxiliary-input ones, from conventional assumptions? The goal is a construction whose extraction holds precisely for these restricted samplers rather than relying on idealized models or knowledge assumptions.
status: Existing approaches via generic-group extraction and constructions based on knowledge assumptions do not resolve this cleaner target. Key works include Campanelli (2026), *A Note on Extractable Witness Encryption in Generic Groups*, ePrint 2026/2399, and Garg et al. (2014), ePrint 2013/860.
solved_when: A construction of extractable witness encryption exists under conventional standard-model assumptions, with extraction provable for a precisely specified class of public-coin or bounded-auxiliary-input samplers.
why: Some applications require that the ability to decrypt implies possession of an actual witness; without a standard-model construction, such applications must fall back on generic-group extraction or knowledge assumptions.
key_works: Campanelli (2026), *A Note on Extractable Witness Encryption in Generic Groups*, ePrint 2026/2399; Garg et al. (2014), ePrint 2013/860.

title: Collision resistance from iO and ordinary OWFs
subfield: Stronger obfuscation notions, auxiliary information, and leakage
open: Construct collision-resistant hashing from iO and arbitrary OWFs without requiring rerandomizable OWFs or another extra primitive.
status: The 2026 rerandomization result obtains collision resistance under a stronger OWF condition.
why: It probes a major unresolved boundary of what iO implies.
key_works: Nassar (2026), *The Power of Rerandomization in Obfustopia*, ePrint 2026/1785; Asharov–Segev (2015), ePrint 2015/341.

bib.title: Collision resistance from iO and ordinary OWFs

title: Leakage-resilient obfuscator generation and execution
subfield: Stronger obfuscation notions, auxiliary information, and leakage
open: Can an obfuscator be generated and executed so that security survives quantified leakage — from the generation randomness, intermediate encodings, execution traces, and repeated physical observations — rather than only in the idealized mathematical setting?
status: Mathematical obfuscation definitions do not automatically cover these implementation interfaces; no such leakage-aware construction is known. Related notions include side-channel noninterference and leakage-resilient computation; see Cousins et al. (2017/2018), *Implementing Conjunction Obfuscation under Entropic Ring LWE*, ePrint 2017/844.
solved_when: An obfuscation scheme is constructed and proven secure under a definition that quantitatively accounts for leakage at each of these implementation interfaces: generation randomness, intermediate encodings, execution traces, and repeated physical observations.
why: A perfectly secure final artifact can still be compromised while being generated or executed, so current guarantees do not protect the artifact in practice.
key_works: Cousins et al. (2017/2018), *Implementing Conjunction Obfuscation under Entropic Ring LWE*, ePrint 2017/844.

title: Standard-model obfuscation of arbitrary quantum channels
subfield: Quantum indistinguishability obfuscation
open: Can arbitrary efficient quantum channels — including genuinely nonunitary ones — be obfuscated in the standard model, with no ideal classical oracle and no random-oracle idealization? More precisely, is there a construction whose security rests on standard, explicitly stated computational assumptions rather than on access to an idealized oracle?
status: The current state of the art is the 2026 arbitrary-channel construction of Huang–Tang (2026), *Obfuscation of Arbitrary Quantum Circuits*, arXiv:2601.08969, which handles arbitrary channels but is an oracle-model result.
solved_when: A construction exists that obfuscates any efficient quantum channel (unitary or nonunitary) and carries a proof of indistinguishability security in the standard model, without an ideal classical oracle or pseudorandom-oracle idealization.
why: It would bring general program secrecy to the full quantum-computation model, covering irreversible and measurement-like operations rather than only the unitary fragment.
key_works: Huang–Tang (2026), *Obfuscation of Arbitrary Quantum Circuits*, arXiv:2601.08969.

bib.title: Standard-model obfuscation of arbitrary quantum channels

title: Classical descriptions of quantum obfuscations without oracle idealization
subfield: Quantum indistinguishability obfuscation
open: Can obfuscated pseudodeterministic quantum circuits be given purely classical, standard-model descriptions under explicit assumptions? The goal is to replace the heuristic oracle idealization with an explicit instantiation.
status: Publicly verifiable QFHE supplies an important oracle-model construction, due to Bartusek–Gupte–Mutreja–Shmueli (2025/2026), *Classical Obfuscation of Quantum Circuits via Publicly-Verifiable QFHE*, arXiv:2510.08400; it does not settle this instantiation problem.
solved_when: A construction is given with a classical description of the obfuscated circuit, proved in the standard model from explicitly stated assumptions, with no oracle substitution.
why: Classical distribution would greatly simplify quantum-software deployment.
key_works: Bartusek–Gupte–Mutreja–Shmueli (2025/2026), *Classical Obfuscation of Quantum Circuits via Publicly-Verifiable QFHE*, arXiv:2510.08400.

bib.title: Classical descriptions of quantum obfuscations without oracle idealization

title: Quantum iO from plain LWE beyond existing barriers
subfield: Quantum indistinguishability obfuscation
open: Can we base a meaningful general notion of quantum indistinguishability obfuscation on plain LWE, using techniques that evade the known barriers? Formally, construct a general quantum-iO variant from plain LWE via reductions outside the classes excluded by the 2026 falsifiable-assumption separation.
status: The 2026 falsifiable-assumption separation of Barhoush–Morimae–Movassagh (2026), *Separating Quantum Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Falsifiable Assumptions* (arXiv:2608.25195), establishes specific interface and reduction restrictions; no construction bypassing them is currently known.
solved_when: A construction of a general quantum-iO variant is given, proved secure under plain LWE by a reduction that does not fall within the interface or reduction restrictions identified by the 2026 barrier.
why: It would tie quantum program secrecy to a conventional, well-studied post-quantum assumption, anchoring quantum obfuscation to standard lattice trust.
key_works: Barhoush–Morimae–Movassagh (2026), *Separating Quantum Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Falsifiable Assumptions*, arXiv:2608.25195.

bib.title: Quantum iO from plain LWE beyond existing barriers

title: Quantum-iO barriers against coherent reductions
subfield: Quantum indistinguishability obfuscation
open: Does the existing separation between quantum indistinguishability obfuscation and falsifiable assumptions still hold when the reduction is allowed coherent quantum queries, rather than only the restricted classical-query interface? A formal answer would either extend the barrier to reductions modeled as quantum query algorithms or exhibit an evasive route.
status: The current separation, due to Barhoush–Morimae–Movassagh (2026) in *Separating Quantum Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Falsifiable Assumptions* (ePrint 2026/1800), applies only to reductions with the restricted classical-query interface, which is a substantive qualification of the barrier.
solved_when: The barrier is shown to persist (or to break) for reductions making coherent quantum queries, rather than only classical-query reductions; this resolves whether the query interface is a genuine limitation of the current impossibility.
why: It tests whether a remaining construction route for quantum iO is genuinely excluded by the barrier, or whether the classical-query restriction leaves that route open.
key_works: Barhoush–Morimae–Movassagh (2026), *Separating Quantum Indistinguishability Obfuscation from Falsifiable Assumptions*, ePrint 2026/1800.

title: Quantum-state ciphertexts and quantum-iO barriers
subfield: Quantum indistinguishability obfuscation
open: Do obfuscation and witness-encryption schemes — or their impossibility — survive when the ciphertext itself is a quantum state? Formally, establish constructions or comparable impossibility results for quantum-state ciphertexts, beyond the classical-ciphertext setting.
status: Existing separations are stated for classical-ciphertext restrictions, leaving the quantum-state ciphertext regime open. Key works: Barhoush–Morimae–Movassagh (2026), arXiv:2608.25195.
solved_when: Either a construction with quantum-state ciphertexts is established, or an impossibility/separation result comparable to the known classical-ciphertext separation is proven for the quantum-ciphertext regime.
why: Quantum information may change the construction landscape, not merely the adversary; restricting to classical ciphertexts leaves a distinct resource regime unexplored.
key_works: Barhoush–Morimae–Movassagh (2026), arXiv:2608.25195.

title: Classical one-wayness from quantum iO
subfield: Quantum indistinguishability obfuscation
open: Does quantum indistinguishability obfuscation give us classical one-way functions under weak worst-case hardness assumptions, rather than merely quantum-state primitives? More precisely, which variants of quantum iO imply classical one-wayness, and which do not?
status: The 2025 classification of Morimae–Shirakawa–Yamakawa (2025/2026), *From Worst-Case Hardness of NP to Quantum Cryptography via Quantum Indistinguishability Obfuscation* (arXiv:2506.19542), proves several quantum consequences from quantum iO; whether classical consequences follow depends on the particular variant.
solved_when: A characterization is given of the quantum-iO variants that imply classical one-way functions under weak worst-case assumptions, identifying for each variant whether the implication holds.
why: It settles whether quantum obfuscation necessarily entails classical cryptographic hardness, sharpening the boundary between quantum-only and classical consequences of iO.
key_works: Morimae–Shirakawa–Yamakawa (2025/2026), *From Worst-Case Hardness of NP to Quantum Cryptography via Quantum Indistinguishability Obfuscation*, arXiv:2506.19542.

title: Single-copy versus multi-copy quantum-iO security
subfield: Quantum indistinguishability obfuscation
open: Does the security of quantum indistinguishability obfuscation degrade as adversaries receive more of the obfuscated state — specifically, what are the implications or separations between access to a single copy of the obfuscation state, polynomially many copies, and coherent (oracle-style) access to an evaluator?
status: These interfaces supply different resources and cannot be identified by classical iO intuition alone; related work includes Morimae–Shirakawa–Yamakawa (2025/2026), arXiv:2506.19542.
solved_when: For each pair among the single-copy, polynomially-many-copies, and coherent-evaluator-access models, an implication or a separation (with proof) between the corresponding quantum-iO security notions is established.
why: A negative answer here means the security of an obfuscated program could silently change the moment protected programs are redistributed, undermining the trust model of obfuscation itself.
key_works: Morimae–Shirakawa–Yamakawa (2025/2026), arXiv:2506.19542.
